answer: Harberger-taxed seats make each identity a priced license: an agent self-assesses its seat value, pays a steady tax on it, and anyone may buy the seat at that price. Cheap seats invite takeover and dear ones burn tax, so N fake heads mean N funded bids, and the rate climbs for seats sharing a funding source. Price lists that mirror each other betray one operator, a whisper heard across the farm, and those seats drift like a dune to real bidders.
